test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 27 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error.

I am working with him since 2002, / but even today / I am unable / to understand his motives.

options.text: I am working with him since 2002,

solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the present perfect continuous tense should be used instead of the present continuous tense.
 
• Since the action of working with him started in the past (in 2002) and continues to the present, the correct tense is **present perfect continuous**.
 
• The correct form should be **"*I have been working with him since 2002*."**

Hence, the correct statement is** "*I have been working with him since 2002__, but even today I am unable to understand his motives."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The present perfect continuous tense is used to show that something started in the past and has continued up until now.
 
• It is formed with **"have/has been" + present participle (verb + ing).**
 
• **Example:** ***She has been reading for two hours.***
